speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started and if there was any specific injury or bite that preceded it? Have you noticed any redness, warmth, or changes in the color of the finger?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you hear a "pop" at the time of injury, and are you able to fully straighten or bend the tip of your finger? I also need to know if there is any numbness or tingling in the finger.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your inability to flex the tip of the finger and the mechanism of injury, this suggests an avulsion of the flexor tendon. REQUEST TEST: X-Ray_right_ring_finger.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray confirms no fracture, which points to a pure tendon injury, likely a Jersey finger. To confirm the diagnosis, I need to see the tendon's position. REQUEST IMAGES.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST IMAGES: Ultrasound_right_ring_finger_flexor_tendon

I need to visualize the retracted flexor digitorum profundus tendon to confirm the avulsion and rule out other soft tissue injuries.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The lack of numbness is reassuring, but the inability to flex the DIP joint with a history of forced extension is classic for a Flexor Digitorum Profundus avulsion, also known as Jersey Finger.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger (Flexor Digitorum Profundus Avulsion)

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
